full_judgment: 2. Plaintiff-respondents instituted the aforesaid suit for declaration of 16 annas title of 'ka' schedule land and further declaration that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 20 of 1995 on 18-7-1996 by the learned Additional Subordinate Judge Narayangonj, to be declared as void, illegal, collusive and not binding upon the plaintiffs. With further declaration that kabala deed in favour of the defendants as mentioned in 'kha schedule to be declared as illegal, fraudulent not acted upon with the averments that the suit land was originally belonged to Ashutosh Chandra Bondhopaddhya and later on, the father of defendant No. 2, Kalu Mia, by a registered deed in 1950 purchased the suit land and thereafter, on amicable partition, defendant No. 2 got absolute title over the suit land. Defendant No. 2 having in need of money, gave out selling of the suit land, to which, plaintiffs agreed and by 12 saf kabalas plaintiffs purchased the suit land on 3-12-87, 6-12-87 and 9-12-87 and after purchase, plaintiffs mutated their names and opened separate khatians and gradually, constructed pucca and kanccha homesteads, giving rents to different tenants and by realizing rents, plaintiffs are enjoying the suit properties. In the first week of July, 1999, plaintiffs found process server of the Court loitering on the suit property. Plaintiff No. 2 came to learn from the process server that defendant No. 1 obtained a decree over the suit property in connivance with men of the Court and wanted to take delivery of the suit property. Plaintiff No. 2 went to Court and through the lawyer, came to know that defendant No. 1 filed Other Class Suit No. 20 of 1995 against defendant No. 2 for specific performance of a contract and obtained a decree by suppressing the real fact and by executing in Title Execution Case No. 4 of 1996, obtained saf kabala deed through court. Plaintiffs getting such knowledge filed an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for staying the proceeding of Title Execution Case No. 4 of 1996 which was fixed for hearing on 28-7-1999. The plaintiffs obtained entire order sheets including the judgment and decree of Title Suit No. 20 of 1995 on 25-7-1999 and came to know that for entire suit land the price of the suit property was fixed at Taka 2,40,000 and after taking Taka 10,000 from defendant No. 1, defendant No. 2 executed bainama on 9-9-1985 and on the strength of the said baina defendant No. 1 filed Title Suit No. 246 of 1987 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, first Court, which was transferred to the Court of Additional Subordinate Judge, first Court and re-numbered as Title Suit No. 20 of 1995, in which defendant No. 2 filed written statement but did not contest the suit and in connivance with defendant No. 1, allowed the suit decreed ex-parte on 18-7-1996. In that suit, defendant No. 2 in written statement stating that the period mentioning in the bainama being expired, defendant No. 1 having not paying the balance consideration money, said baina was cancelled and defendant No. 2 sold the property to different persons. Plaintiffs being subsequent purchasers with valuable consideration without notice of the alleged bainapatra and having been in possession of the suit land from 3-12-1987 by constructing pucca, semipucca structure on the suit land but defendant No. 1 obtained decree in Title Suit No.20 of 1995 stating in the plaint that defendant No. 1 is in possession of the suit land from 9-9-1985 and obtained the aforesaid decree fraudulently.
